CRITICAL field bug, reported by Elton directly from a live session ('package 117 is still a broken piece of shit') and diagnosed from his own uploaded session_2026-09-30_19-06-34.* logs. Root cause: do_search_text() (lib_bejson_newagent_actions.py) shelled out to ripgrep with NO output cap and NO directory exclusions -- a `search_text bookwriter` call matched into logs/ (archived session transcripts containing nested escaped JSON from prior sessions) and returned 1,954,412 bytes raw, which got force-fed into the very next turn's context and persisted into the session's own logs -- exactly why the uploaded .md/.bejson logs were themselves ~2MB after only 2 turns. Fixed with -g exclusions (logs/, backups/, .git/, __pycache__/, node_modules/) plus a new 64KB output cap (_cap_subprocess_output(), matching do_http_get/do_read_file's existing caps) applied to do_search_text, do_find_files, and do_fuzzy_find -- the only three subprocess-backed actions that had no cap at all. SECOND bug found verifying the first: the -g exclusion globs silently did not work, because ripgrep anchors a relative glob to the search-root ARGUMENT's own relative structure, and the code passed an absolute resolved path with no cwd= set -- confirmed directly via a minimal repro (`rg -g '!logs/**' pat /abs/path` still matches inside /abs/path/logs/). Fixed by running the subprocess with cwd= set to the search root and a relative target. lib_bejson_newagent_actions.py: 2.3.1 (header had drifted behind the live VERSION=2.4.0 constant, untracked, realigned without guessing at the missing gap) -> 2.5.0. SEPARATE finding, same investigation, NOT a code bug: diagnosed why the agent launched into unprompted file exploration in response to a bare 'hi' -- Context/Persistent_Policy.md's own 'Job system rule' says 'never bring up jobs on your own initiative', but build_active_tasks_section() in context_bubble.py auto-surfaces ANY checklist_*.bejson file with incomplete tasks into '## Active Tasks' every turn BY DESIGN (Amnesia-proofing, per its own docstring), which the model then correctly acted on per its instructions for an 'active job'. Root cause was a design conflict between two parts of the same policy text, not a code defect. Inspected the actual flagged checklist (checklist_integrate_ai_libs_into_cli_bookwriter.bejson) before acting on it rather than deleting it as first proposed: it's genuine recent work (created 2026-09-14, 4 of 6 tasks done, 2 genuinely pending) -- deleting it would have destroyed real progress tracking to patch around a triggering bug. Left the checklist alone; fixed the actual behavior instead by adding a 'Checklist rule' paragraph to Persistent_Policy.md distinguishing checklists (auto-surfaced, informational) from jobs (/jobstart-initiated), instructing the model to address what the user actually said first and only mention an open checklist rather than unilaterally acting on it, unless the user's message is actually about it. Verified new text fits comfortably within the pct_persistent_policy budget (2838 of 6400 chars) and reads correctly through _read_policy().
